what_its_for: Secukinumab is used to treat certain conditions where your immune system attacks your own body. These include moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (red, scaly skin patches), psoriatic arthritis (joint pain and swelling linked to psoriasis), ankylosing spondylitis (spine inflammation and stiffness), non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (back and joint inflammation), and nr-axSpA. It works by blocking a protein in your body called IL-17A that causes inflammation.
how_to_take: Secukinumab is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your stomach area, thigh, or upper outer arm. It comes in a pre-filled pen (Sensoready Pen) or a pre-filled syringe. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to give yourself the injection at home. Always rotate injection sites and never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or hard. Let the pen or syringe warm to room temperature for 15 to 30 minutes before injecting. Do not shake the device.
dosing: Your dose depends on your condition. For plaque psoriasis in adults, a common schedule is 300 mg once a week for 5 weeks (called the loading dose), then 300 mg once every 4 weeks (maintenance dose). For psoriatic arthritis or ankylosing spondylitis, the dose is often 150 mg on the same schedule, though your doctor may start you at 300 mg. Your doctor will decide the exact dose and schedule that is right for you. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then go back to your regular schedule. If your next scheduled dose is very soon, skip the missed dose and continue on your normal schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store secukinumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. You may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 4 days if needed, but after that it must be thrown away. Do not put it back in the refrigerator after it has been kept at room temperature. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens and syringes in a sharps container — do not throw them in the trash.
what_to_avoid: Avoid receiving live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using secukinumab, as they may cause infection. Tell all your doctors and dentists that you take this medicine before any procedures or new vaccines. Avoid close contact with people who have active infections. Avoid activities that may increase your risk of getting sick if possible.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any of the following: signs of infection such as fever, chills, cough, shortness of breath, burning when urinating, or a wound that will not heal; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, dizziness, or trouble breathing; new or worsening bowel problems such as stomach cramps, diarrhea with blood, or mucus in stool (which could be signs of inflammatory bowel disease); feeling very tired or unwell; or any new symptoms that concern you. Do not ignore signs of infection, as this medicine lowers your ability to fight certain germs.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within a few weeks, but it can take up to 3 to 4 months to see the full benefit of the medicine. Do not stop taking it even if you feel better, unless your doctor tells you to. Stopping suddenly may cause your symptoms to return.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not fully known whether secukinumab is safe during pregnancy or breastfeeding. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 20 weeks after your last dose. Children: Secukinumab is approved for children 6 years and older for certain conditions such as plaque psoriasis and enthesitis-related arthritis. The dose for children is based on their weight, and a doctor will determine the right amount. Older adults: Older patients may use secukinumab, but should be watched closely for signs of infection. Kidney or liver problems: No dose changes are usually needed, but always tell your doctor about all your health conditions.
